Если бы Генри или Фрэнсис произнёс своё впечатление вслух, он назвал бы её самой округлой из всех худых женщин, каких ему доводилось видеть.", "source_sha256": "f701e6ef6c798b0db75b0687a1d3573254cdfe14463344da4905598aee3818fd", "target_id": "ru-ru78-u020-r0030", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "0e559421a5b20aff1063766d5352a140d81c3eed5551a6f4bedc57268ba21fee"}, {"source_id": "ru78-u020-r0031", "target": "Жрец Солнца простёр свой дряхлый стан, пока не распростёрся плашмя на полу, зарывшись старым лбом в травяную циновку. Остальные остались стоять, хотя Торрес по подгибавшимся коленям показал, что последовал бы примеру жреца, если бы его спутники выказали намерение сделать то же. Так что колени его частично подогнулись, но снова выпрямились и закоченели под сдержанным примером Леонсии и Морганов.", "source_sha256": "299bf27e90fee88b83d635386fe82c77918321da1007826f2dcdfb154dc6775d", "target_id": "ru-ru78-u020-r0031", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "f3b9a3b38cdb68f43c3871e6bca0fee4f0e908e157138ee58cf913f8b7475ad8"}]}, "source_rows": [{"id": "ru78-u020-r0032", "tag": "p", "text": "At first the Lady had no eyes for aught but Leoncia; and, after a careful looking over of her, with a curt upward lift of head she commanded her to approach. So she did not move, until the Sun Priest muttered harshly that she must obey. She approached, regardless of the huge, long-haired hound, threading between the tripods and past the beast, nor would stop until commanded by a second nod as curt as the first. For a long minute the two women gazed steadily into each other’s eyes, at the end of which, with a flicker of triumph, Leoncia observed the other’s eyes droop. But the flicker was temporary, for Leoncia saw that the Lady was studying her dress with haughty curiosity. She even reached out her slender, pallid hand and felt the texture of the cloth and caressed it as only a woman can.", "sha256": "c60f46c26afb65e17bf8345e28a2a109ac6b372a775118b7c89df536fcc8e3d8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[1673]", "source_html": "

At first the Lady had no eyes for aught but Leoncia; and, after a careful looking over of her, with a curt upward lift of head she commanded her to approach. Too imperative by far was it, in Leoncia’s thought, to proceed from so etherially beautiful a creature, and she sensed with immediacy an antagonism that must exist between them. So she did not move, until the Sun Priest muttered harshly that she must obey. She approached, regardless of the huge, long-haired hound, threading between the tripods and past the beast, nor would stop until commanded by a second nod as curt as the first. For a long minute the two women gazed steadily into each other’s eyes, at the end of which, with a flicker of triumph, Leoncia observed the other’s eyes droop. But the flicker was temporary, for Leoncia saw that the Lady was studying her dress with haughty curiosity. She even reached out her slender, pallid hand and felt the texture of the cloth and caressed it as only a woman can.

“That on this day strange events were to occur. They have occurred, O Queen.”

", "emphasis_spans": 0}, {"id": "ru78-u020-r0039", "tag": "p", "text": "“I have seen you before, and often,” the Queen went on.", "sha256": "2beb010124f386c80c758237908b2b48581f220008d673e9399a2ccef7d4bea8", "source_xpath": "/html/body/p[1680]", "source_html": "
